name: Beaufort County Schools
subject: Beaufort County Schools: your email domain can currently be spoofed (free 20-minute fix inside)
body:
Hello,

I'm a high school senior in Cary. As an independent project, I checked the public email-security records of every NC school district and municipality, 609 in total, using standard DNS lookups. Nothing was sent to or accessed on your systems; these records are public by design.

Here is what I found for Beaufort County Schools:

beaufort.k12.nc.us has no DMARC record at all.

What that means in practice: an email forged to look like it came from an @beaufort.k12.nc.us address would not be rejected by the recipient's mail server. This is how business email compromise works, where a fake message from a director or manager asks a clerk to change a vendor's bank details. It is the most expensive category of cybercrime the FBI tracks, and local governments and school districts are frequent targets.

You are not alone: 68% of NC public bodies are in the same position.

The fix is free and takes about twenty minutes. The safe first step (monitoring mode) changes nothing about how your mail works today:

  Host:  _dmarc.beaufort.k12.nc.us
  Type:  TXT
  Value: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@beaufort.k12.nc.us; fo=1

After a few weeks of reports, the policy can move to p=quarantine and then p=reject, which is what CISA recommends for government domains. Full step-by-step instructions: [GITHUB LINK]

If it would help, I'm glad to answer questions. I'll be re-checking all 609 domains in about thirty days to see how many have been secured, and I'd be glad to count yours.

I'm a high school senior in Cary. As an independent project, I checked the public email-security records of every NC school district and municipality, 609 in total, using standard DNS lookups. Nothing was sent to or accessed on your systems; these records are public by design.

Here is what I found for Grantsboro:

grantsboronc.com has no DMARC record at all. (Your staff mail runs on embarqmail.com, which is fine; this is about the town's own domain.)

What that means in practice: anyone can send an email that appears to come from an @grantsboronc.com address, and nothing tells the recipient it's fake. Attackers use unused domains exactly this way. This is how business email compromise works, where a fake message from a director or manager asks a clerk to change a vendor's bank details. It is the most expensive category of cybercrime the FBI tracks, and local governments and school districts are frequent targets.

You are not alone: 68% of NC public bodies are in the same position.

The fix is free and takes about twenty minutes. The safe first step (monitoring mode) changes nothing about how your mail works today:

  Host:  _dmarc.grantsboronc.com
  Type:  TXT
  Value: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@grantsboronc.com; fo=1

After a few weeks of reports, the policy can move to p=quarantine and then p=reject, which is what CISA recommends for government domains. Full step-by-step instructions: [GITHUB LINK]

If it would help, I'm glad to answer questions. I'll be re-checking all 609 domains in about thirty days to see how many have been secured, and I'd be glad to count yours.
